clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old girl presents with 3 weeks of right-sided headache and horizontal binocular diplopia. An ophthalmologist diagnoses right cranial nerve VI palsy. Brain MRI with and without gadolinium is normal. CSF studies show normal cell counts, no malignant cells, normal meningitis PCR panel, negative cultures, no oligoclonal bands, and normal ACE and lysozyme; serum protein electrophoresis and autoimmune and infectious serologies are normal. Neurological status remains stable throughout admission, and negative CSF cytology and serum protein electrophoresis results exclude neoplastic processes such as lymphoma. The diagnosis of an idiopathic inflammatory process (Tolosa-Hunt syndrome) is made.
